answer: Nonce-Expiring Identity Claim. Each agent identity is a keypair whose first transaction must embed a unique, recently issued challenge nonce tied to a live physical beacon (e.g. a wharf sensor timestamp, a tundra station reading, or a comet observation window). The beacon signs only one claim per nonce, and nonces expire in minutes. An attacker cannot reuse a captured claim, must obtain fresh beacon signatures for every identity, and each attempt consumes a distinct scarce beacon slot, forcing a real per-identity cost in access and latency.
